Ziply Fiber is a local internet service provider dedicated to elevating the connected lives of the communities we serve. We offer the fastest home internet in the nation, a refreshingly great customer experience, and affordable plans that put customers in charge.

As our state-of-the-art fiber network expands, so does our need for team members who can help us grow and realize our goals.

Our Company Values:

  • Genuinely Caring:We treat customers and colleagues like neighbors, with empathy and full attention.
  • Empowering You:We help customers choose what is best for them, and we support employees in implementing new ideas and solutions.
  • Innovation and Improvement:We constantly seek ways to improve how we serve customers and each other.
  • Earning Your Trust:We build trust through clear, honest, human communication.

Job Summary

Ziply Fiber's competitive advantage is fiber — and fiber starts with transport. The Principal Architect for Transport is the technical authority for Ziply's physical layer backbone: the dark fiber routes, long-haul rings, DWDM infrastructure, and data center interconnects that carry every bit we deliver. You will define transport topology, drive capacity planning, architect the infrastructure that enables Ziply's expansion into adjacent and edge-out markets and own the co-location strategy that positions us at the right interconnection points across the Pacific Northwest and beyond.

This is a hands-on senior independent contributor role for a transport architect who thinks in fiber strands, route diversity, and wavelength economics — and who has the project management discipline to take a transport program from route survey through cutover.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

The Essential Duties and Responsibilities listed below are a range of duties performed by the employee and not intended to reflect all duties performed.

Dark Fiber & Long-Haul Architecture

●Design and own Ziply's long-haul and regional dark fiber route architecture: ring topology, route diversity, redundancy standards, and failure domain analysis.

●Define fiber route acquisition strategy: IRU evaluation criteria, route survey requirements, and technical due diligence for new fiber agreements.

●Maintain authoritative transport network documentation: route inventories, fiber maps, strand assignments, splice records, and capacity databases.

●Own OTDR testing standards, fiber acceptance criteria, and ongoing plant performance monitoring.

DWDM & Optical Layer

●Architect DWDM and coherent optical infrastructure: platform selection (Ciena, Infinera, Nokia, or equivalent), ROADM degree planning, and wavelength engineering for long-haul and metro rings.

●Define optical capacity planning: traffic forecasting, wavelength utilization thresholds, fiber exhaust modeling, and upgrade trigger criteria.

●Own OTN/FlexGrid transport architecture: framing standards, multiplexing hierarchy, and protection switching (OLP, OSNCP, or equivalent).

●Evaluate open line system and disaggregated optical architectures (OpenROADM, OpenConfig optical) for cost and operational fit.

Data Center Interconnect & Co-location

●Architect data center interconnect (DCI) strategy: wavelength engineering, low-latency path design, and capacity scaling between Ziply facilities and third-party co-location sites.

●Define co-location strategy: meet-me room presence, cross-connect standards, and third-party peering and transit interconnect infrastructure.

●Manage relationships with co-location providers: SLA governance, capacity planning, and commercial terms aligned to Ziply's network growth roadmap.

Market Expansion & Capacity Planning

●Architect transport infrastructure requirements for adjacent market expansion and edge-out programs: route planning, capacity dimensioning, and build sequencing.

●Own transport capacity planning across the network: traffic matrix modeling, link utilization monitoring, and proactive upgrade planning to stay ahead of demand.

●Partner with Network Planning on transport inputs for new market entry decisions: fiber availability, route cost, and build vs. lease analysis.

●Collaborate with IP Core & Metro architects to ensure transport and IP layer integration is optimized for performance, resilience, and cost efficiency.

Other Duties

·Performs other duties as required to support the business and evolving organization.

Required Qualifications:

·High school diploma or GED.

·Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Telecommunications, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and directly relevant transport architecture experience.

·10+ years of transport network engineering, optical networking, backbone infrastructure, or carrier transport experience within an ISP, CLEC, fiber network operator, telecommunications provider, regional carrier, or similar network-intensive environment.Demonstrated senior independent contributor experience setting transport architecture standards, influencing technical direction, mentoring engineers, and driving cross-functional architecture decisions without direct people-management responsibility.

·Deep expertise in DWDM/ROADM platforms: Ciena, Infinera, Nokia, or equivalent — architecture, commissioning, and operations of coherent optical systems.

·Strong dark fiber operations background: IRU agreements, fiber route management, OTDR testing, splice documentation, and fiber plant acceptance.

·Experience with transport capacity planning and traffic engineering at regional or national scale: traffic matrix modeling, wavelength utilization, and fiber exhaust forecasting.

·Solid OTN/FlexGrid architecture knowledge: framing, multiplexing, protection schemes, and optical performance monitoring.

·Experience with co-location and DCI strategy: meet-me room operations, cross-connect management, and carrier interconnection.

·Excellent technical documentation skills; able to maintain authoritative route and capacity records and communicate complex topology decisions to non-technical stakeholders.

·Experience creating architecture decision records, reference designs, transport standards, route-diversity frameworks, operational runbooks, capacity planning frameworks, and governance processes for production transport, optical, dark fiber, DCI, or co-location infrastructure.

Preferred Qualifications:

●Experience with open line systems and disaggregated optical networking: OpenROADM, OpenConfig optical, or vendor-neutral DWDM deployments.

●Background in fiber route acquisition: IRU negotiations, route survey, and technical due diligence for new fiber agreements.

●Familiarity with GIS-based network documentation and fiber management systems.

●Experience with transport network automation: NETCONF/YANG, gNMI, or optical controller platforms (Ciena MCP, Nokia NSP, or equivalent).

●Prior experience supporting competitive market expansion or fiber overbuilder programs.

●Experience presenting transport, optical, co-location, route-diversity, capacity, or expansion strategy to VP-level or executive audiences.

●Experience with business continuity planning, facility resiliency, critical infrastructure risk assessment, or physical route-diversity governance for transport networks.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

·Ability to work independently and apply sound judgment and reasoning skills to a variety of situations.

·Ability to multi-task and collaborate effectively with other personnel to meet deadlines.

·Strong verbal and written communication, attention to detail, and organizational skills.

·Ability to work within critical deadlines.

·Ability to adjust to rapidly changing priorities and schedules.

·Ability to provide excellent customer service.

·Senior technical leadership skills with the ability to influence transport architecture, mentor technical teams, establish standards, and build alignment without direct people-management authority.

·Strong analytical and systems-thinking skills with the ability to balance resiliency, scalability, route diversity, optical performance, operational supportability, cost, market expansion, and business continuity risk.

·Executive presence and communication skills to explain complex transport architecture decisions clearly and credibly to Technology, Operations, Finance, Legal, Procurement, Construction, vendors, and senior leadership.

Work Authorization

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the US for any employer. Sponsorship is not available for this position.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Essential and marginal functions may require maintaining physical condition necessary for bending, stooping, sitting, walking, or standing for prolonged periods of time; most of time is spent sitting in a comfortable position with frequent opportunity to move about. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

Work Environment

Work is performed in an office setting with exposure to computer screens and requires extensive use of a computer, keyboard, mouse, and multi-line telephone system. The work is primarily a modern office setting.

The Team:

The Product Marketing team at Turnitin is curious, customer-centric, data-driven, and collaborative. We’re responsible for the global go-to-market strategy for Turnitin’s portfolio of academic integrity and assessment solutions. The team collaborates cross-functionally with product management, corporate marketing, demand marketing, and global sales to develop positioning and messaging, content assets, campaigns, and sales tools in support of product revenue and customer engagement goals. The team is also responsible for competitive analysis and positioning.

The Role:

We are seeking an experienced Product Marketing Manager to lead how we communicate our approach to data privacy, security, AI and data use, and accessibility to customers and the broader market.

This role sits at the intersection of Product, Security, Privacy/Legal, AI, Accessibility, Sales, and Marketing. You will translate complex technical and policy topics into clear, credible, customer-friendly messaging that builds trust and helps customers understand how we protect their data, use AI responsibly, and design accessible products.

The ideal candidate has 5–7 years of experience in product marketing, product management, technology marketing, or a related field, preferably within B2B SaaS, education technology, enterprise software, or another highly regulated or trust-sensitive environment.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and maintain clear market-facing positioning and messaging for data privacy, security, AI data use, responsible AI practices, and accessibility across our product portfolio.
  • Communicate How We Use Customer Data: Clearly articulate how customer and user data is collected, processed, stored, protected, retained, and used within our products, partnering closely with Privacy, Legal, Security, and Product teams to ensure accuracy.
  • Lead AI Transparency Communications: Own customer-facing communications explaining where and how AI is used across our products, what data AI features access, how that data is handled, and whether and under what circumstances customer data is used to train or improve AI models.
  • Maintain External Trust & Transparency Resources: Own and continuously improve external-facing web content and resources that provide customers with easy-to-understand information about our security, privacy, AI, data-use, and accessibility practices.
  • Translate Technical Concepts for Customers: Turn complex security architectures, privacy practices, AI technologies, accessibility standards, and regulatory requirements into language that customers, educators, administrators, procurement teams, and business leaders can readily understand.
  • Enable Sales and Customer-Facing Teams: Develop training, playbooks, FAQs, objection-handling guidance, presentations, and talk tracks that help Sales, Customer Success, and other customer-facing teams confidently discuss security, privacy, AI data use, and accessibility.
  • Support Customer and Procurement Conversations: Partner with Sales, Security, Privacy, Legal, and Product teams to address common customer questions and concerns arising during evaluations, procurement processes, security reviews, and renewals.
  • Create a Consistent Source of Truth: Establish and maintain approved messaging so that Product, Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Legal, Privacy, and Security communicate consistently about these topics.
  • Partner on Product Launches: Ensure new products and features—particularly those involving AI or new uses of customer data—have appropriate trust, privacy, security, and accessibility messaging as part of launch readiness.
  • Drive Proactive Customer Communication: Identify emerging topics that may create customer questions or concerns and develop proactive communications before they become barriers to adoption or renewal.
  • Monitor the Market and Regulatory Landscape: Stay informed about evolving expectations and regulations related to AI, privacy, security, and accessibility and help translate those developments into implications for product positioning and customer communication.
  • Represent the Voice of the Customer: Bring recurring customer questions and concerns back to Product, Security, Privacy, Legal, and Accessibility teams to influence product decisions, policies, documentation, and roadmap priorities.

What success looks like:

Customers can quickly understand how we protect their data, how AI is used in our products, whether their data is used to train AI models, and how we approach accessibility. Sales and Customer Success teams can confidently answer these questions without unnecessarily escalating routine inquiries, and our external communications consistently reinforce trust in our products and company.

  • 5–7 years of experience in product marketing, product management, technology marketing, or a related B2B SaaS role.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate highly technical or regulated topics into clear, compelling customer-facing communications.
  • Experience partnering with Product, Engineering, Security, Legal/Privacy, Sales, and Customer Success organizations.
  • Strong understanding of SaaS data privacy and security concepts; familiarity with AI governance, responsible AI, and accessibility is highly desirable.
  • Experience developing sales enablement programs, messaging frameworks, FAQs, competitive materials, or customer-facing product documentation.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Comfortable navigating topics where technical capabilities, regulatory requirements, customer expectations, and market positioning intersect.
  • Ability to build credibility with technical and legal subject-matter experts while maintaining a strong customer and commercial perspective.
  • Must be able to regularly flex schedule across global time zones to further One Team collaboration and execute within a global function.

Total Rewards @ Turnitin
At Turnitin, we believe Total Rewards go far beyond pay. While salary, bonus, or commission are important, they’re only part of the value you receive in exchange for your work.

Beyond compensation, you’ll experience the intrinsic rewards of unleashing your potential and making a positive impact on global education. You’ll also thrive in a culture free of politics, surrounded by humble, inclusive, and collaborative teammates.

In addition, our extrinsic rewards include generous time off and health and wellness programs that provide choice, flexibility, and a safety net for life’s challenges. You’ll also enjoy a remote-first culture that empowers you to work with purpose and accountability in the way that suits you best, all supported by a comprehensive package that prioritizes your overall well-being.

Our Mission is to ensure the integrity of global education and meaningfully improve learning outcomes.

Our Values underpin everything we do.

  • Customer Centric: Our mission is focused on improving learning outcomes; we do this by putting educators and learners at the center of everything we do.
  • Passion for Learning: We are committed to our own learning and growth internally. And we support education and learning around the globe.
  • Integrity: Integrity is the heartbeat of Turnitin—it is the core of our products, the way we treat each other, and how we work with our customers and vendors.
  • Action & Ownership: We have a bias for action. We act like owners. We are willing to change even when it’s hard.
  • One Team: We strive to break down silos, collaborate effectively, and celebrate each others' successes.
  • Global Mindset: We consider different perspectives and celebrate diversity. We are one team. The work we do has an impact on the world.

Global Benefits

  • Education Reimbursement*

  • Monthly Wellness or Home Office Reimbursement/*
  • Access to Modern Health (mental health platform)

  • Retirement Plan with match/contribution*

* varies by country

Seeing Beyond the Job Ad
At Turnitin, we recognize it’s unrealistic for candidates to fulfill 100% of the criteria in a job ad. We encourage you to apply if you meet the majority of the requirements because we know that skills evolve over time. If you’re willing to learn and unleash your potential alongside us, join our team!

When you join Turnitin, you'll be welcomed into a company that is a recognized innovator in the global education space. For more than 25 years, Turnitin has partnered with educational institutions to promote honesty, consistency, and fairness across all subject areas and assessment types. Turnitin products are used by educational institutions and certification and licensing programs to uphold integrity and increase learning performance, and by students and professionals to do their best, original work.

Experience a remote-first culture that empowers you to work with purpose and accountability in a way that best suits you, supported by a comprehensive package that prioritizes your overall well-being. jobs.description:
CircusTrix dba

Sky Zone

Incident Investigation Analyst

Full-Time

Hybrid in Dallas, TX, or Remote in O&O States

Department: Risk & Safety

Reports to: Director, Safety

Travel: <10%

FLSA: Exempt

ABOUT US:

CircusTrix is the leading indoor active entertainment company in the U.S., operating and franchising over 270 parks with more than 500,000 members and 60+ attractions. We create fun, high-energy experiences for all ages while hosting thousands of memorable birthdays, team events, and school parties each year. Recognized by Franchise Times and Entrepreneur, our success is driven by a culture of curiosity, creativity, and growth. At Sky Zone, we empower builders, problem-solvers, and lifelong learners to explore bold ideas, challenge assumptions, and make a meaningful impact—creating a place where imagination thrives and people are inspired to grow.

JOB SUMMARY:

The Incident Investigation Analyst is responsible for the end-to-end management of guest injury incident investigations. The Incident Investigation Analyst is responsible for reviewing incident reports within the Risk Management Information System (RMIS) to ensure they are complete, accurate, and compliant with company standards and underwriting requirements. This role conducts and independently leads comprehensive investigations to establish the facts surrounding incidents, identify root causes and contributing factors, and perform quantitative and qualitative analyses to detect patterns, trends, and emerging risks across the organization.

Using incident data and investigative findings, the Incident Investigation Analyst develops actionable insights and recommends corrective and preventive measures to reduce risk, improve operational safety, and support continuous improvement initiatives. This position prepares objective, well-documented investigative reports and collaborates with cross-functional stakeholders to drive risk mitigation strategies while supporting underwriting requirements, claims management, regulatory compliance, and legal defense efforts when necessary.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Incident Auditing & Verification

  • Review and triage all field submitted incident reports relating to guest injury incidents to determine investigation requirements, case priority, and appropriate next steps.
  • Escalate complex, high-risk, or severe incidents to Risk Management, Safety, Legal, or executive leadership, as appropriate.
  • Maintain confidentiality while handling privileged and sensitive incident information in partnership with legal.

Incident Investigation & Documentation

  • Conduct comprehensive investigations of guest injury incidents by gathering, reviewing, and evaluating source documentation including incident reports, witness statements, photographs, surveillance video, maintenance records, inspection logs, operational records, training records, and other supporting evidence, when required.
  • Analyze investigative findings to determine the sequence of events, root cause(s), contributing factors, and potential operational or environmental risks.
  • Maintain complete and accurate investigation records within the organization's Risk Management Information System (RMIS) and other applicable systems.

Root Cause Analysis & Corrective Action Management

  • Perform root cause and contributing factor analyses utilizing established investigative methodologies and best practices.
  • Develop recommendations for corrective and preventive actions designed to reduce future risk and improve operational performance.
  • Issue recommended corrective actions to park leadership and operational departments based on investigation findings.
  • Track corrective actions through completion, ensuring accountability, timely implementation, and proper documentation.

Park Follow-Up & Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for park leadership throughout the investigation process.
  • Follow up with parks to obtain outstanding documentation, investigation updates, corrective action status, and supporting evidence.
  • Provide guidance to park leadership regarding investigation expectations, documentation standards, and corrective action requirements.
  • Facilitate communication between corporate and field teams to support consistent incident management practices.

Data Analysis & Reporting

  • Identify recurring trends, systemic issues, and opportunities for process improvement through analysis of investigation findings and other internal sources.
  • Collaborate in the development of reports and dashboards by providing analysis and insights related to incident activity, investigation performance, corrective action status, and emerging risks.
  • Support leadership by providing data-driven recommendations to improve safety performance and operational effectiveness.

Guest & Stakeholder Communication

  • Contact injured guests, witnesses, or other involved parties when additional information or clarification is required to support investigations.
  • Conduct professional, objective, and empathetic interviews while maintaining neutrality and confidentiality.
  • Respond to internal requests regarding investigation status, documentation, and case information.
  • Deliver exceptional customer service while balancing investigative responsibilities and organizational objectives.

Process Improvement & Compliance

  • Participate in quality assurance reviews to improve investigation consistency, documentation quality, and case management processes.
  • Recommend enhancements to incident reporting, investigation procedures, corrective action tracking, and workflow efficiency.
  • Support OSHA recordkeeping, documentation requests, and other regulatory reporting requirements as applicable.
  • Assist with special projects related to injury prevention, claims support, operational risk reduction, and enterprise safety initiatives.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Risk Management, Occupational Safety, Business Administration, Criminal Justice, Public Administration, or a related field preferred.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in safety compliance, risk management, claims coordination, or insurance litigation support, or a related field.
  • Experience conducting investigations involving injuries, accidents, or operational incidents preferred.
  • Experience in hospitality, amusement parks, entertainment, recreation, retail, or other high-volume customer environments is preferred.
  • Associate Safety Professional (ASP), Associate in Risk Management (ARM), OSHA 30 Certification, or Other relevant investigation, claims, or safety certifications, preferred
  • Analytical Capabilities: Strong foundational skills in accident investigation, root cause analysis and operational risk assessment are preferred.
  • Judgement and Decision Making: Ability to exercise independent judgment and discretion in evaluating complex information, interpreting policies and regulations, assessing operational and liability risk, determining investigative priorities, and making sound risk-based recommendations with minimal supervision.
  • Technical Skills: Demonstrable experience in using software to record and analyze data, including the ability to conceive of and generate reports that generate actionable insights. Proficiency with RMIS or safety management software is preferred, as is an intermediate-level proficiency with Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.
  • Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills are required, with the ability to collaborate professionally with park management to meet documentation timelines and requirements.
  • Attention to Detail: High-level attention to detail regarding documentation and file management is required.
  • Core Competencies: Ability to manage multiple investigations simultaneously while meeting deadlines.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Primarily sedentary work requiring prolonged periods of sitting and routine use of a computer, keyboard, mouse, and multiple monitors.
  • Ability to communicate effectively and exchange accurate information via telephone, video conferencing, email, and in person, as needed.
  • Ability to review, analyze, and interpret electronic records, photographs, videos, reports, and other investigative documentation.
  • Ability to occasionally travel to company parks, corporate offices, or other business locations to conduct investigations, meetings, training, or other business-related activities.
  • Ability to maintain a safe and productive remote work environment that supports the effective performance of essential job duties.
  • Ability to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Compensation rangeis $75,000-$85,000 + bonus opportunity, based on qualifications, experience, and performance. Full-time employees at CircusTrix enjoy a competitive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage along with a 401k plan with company matching. Eligibility for 401k is based on age and tenure requirements.

Application deadline: September 11, 2026

While we anticipate the application window will close on this date, Sky Zone reviews applications on a rolling basis and will continue to consider candidates until the position is filled. As a result, the posting may remain up beyond the stated deadline, but will not be removed before this date.

jobs.description:
Paid Media Specialist / Sr. Paid Media Specialist

Growth & Lifecycle Marketing | Full-Time, Exempt | Reports to Director of Growth & Lifecycle Marketing

Own the paid channels that turn ad dollars into subscribers.

Company Seeking.com (Reflex Media)

Location Remote (US).

Compensation $70,000 to $120,000 base, commensurate with experience and level

Travel Required for team meetings, offsites, shoots, and project needs

About the Role

Seeking.com is the world's largest premium dating platform, and we are entering the most important chapter of our brand transformation. We are looking for a Paid Media Specialist to own paid acquisition end-to-end as a hands-on operator across Google, Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Snapchat, Pinterest, LinkedIn, and any new channel worth opening.

This role is open at two levels: Paid Media Specialist and Sr. Paid Media Specialist. Level and placement in the salary band are determined by experience, demonstrated ownership of large budgets, and depth in the platforms and measurement stack outlined below. The role is the same shape at both levels; the Senior level carries broader scope, more autonomy, and higher expectations on strategy and mentorship.

This role may also be a fit for candidates whose current title is Digital Media Buyer, Media Buyer, Sr. Media Buyer, Performance Marketing Specialist, Paid Acquisition Specialist, Growth Marketing Specialist, Paid Search Specialist, Paid Social Specialist, Performance Media Specialist, Digital Advertising Specialist, or SEM/Paid Media Specialist. If your day-to-day is buying, optimizing, and measuring paid campaigns for a consumer brand, you should apply regardless of your current title.

You will build the campaigns, structure the accounts, ship the ads, read the numbers, and rewrite the plan by Friday. You will report to the Director of Growth & Lifecycle Marketing and partner closely with Creative, Data & Analytics, Product, and Lifecycle.

We are looking for a builder who can log into every ad platform in week one, identify the wasted spend and the missed opportunities, and ship a better-structured campaign by Friday.

What You'll Own

Campaign Build, Optimization & Budget Management

  • Own the day-to-day build and management of paid campaigns across Google Ads (Search, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube), Meta, TikTok, Snapchat, Pinterest, LinkedIn, and any additional platforms worth testing.
  • Structure accounts for scale: campaign taxonomy, ad-group logic, audience layers, bidding strategy, naming conventions, and asset organization.
  • Perform daily optimization across every active account: bid adjustments, negatives, audience pruning, budget reallocation, and creative rotation to hold or improve target CPA, ROAS, and payback.
  • Manage monthly spend at the $250K+ level with the discipline to scale up when performance holds and pull back before CPA breaks.
  • Deploy advanced bidding strategies (tCPA, tROAS, Advantage+, PMax, value-based) with a clear point of view on when to let the machine run and when to override it.
  • Serve as the primary liaison with ad platform reps: secure beta access, resolve policy escalations, unlock account suspensions quickly.

Tracking, Attribution & Analytics

  • Own end-to-end event tracking and conversion setup across GTM, GA4, server-side infrastructure, MMP/attribution tools (Datahash, PostHog, or similar), and platform pixels/CAPIs.
  • Enforce tracking discipline: clean UTMs, correct conversion events, deduplicated pixels, and a documented measurement plan before every launch.
  • Read your own dashboards. Pull your own cuts in Looker, Tableau, or the warehouse. Translate ROAS, CPA, CTR, CPC, and CPM into LTV, CAC, payback, and contribution margin for leadership.

Creative Testing & Iteration

  • Run a continuous testing engine on ad copy, hooks, static and video creative, thumbnails, and landing-page pairings. Weekly at minimum.
  • Brief the Creative team with precision: performance data, competitor references, hypothesis, format specs, clear success metrics. Own the feedback loop.
  • Beat creative fatigue proactively. Track CTR decay, frequency, and cost curves per creative and rotate before performance drops.

Growth Strategy & Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Recommend channel-mix strategy and monthly budget shape. Bring a point of view on where the next incremental subscriber comes from cheapest.
  • Support upper-funnel media planning, measurement, and testing, including YouTube, connected TV, and select traditional/OOH tests when the business case is there.
  • Partner cleanly with the Lifecycle Marketing & CRM Manager, the Growth Experimentation Manager, and the Head of Web so paid, on-site, and lifecycle feel like one continuous conversation to the member.
  • Run competitor intelligence (Meta Ad Library, TikTok Creative Center, SEMrush, SimilarWeb). Know who is winning in the category and what we should steal, remix, or beat.

Required Qualifications (Both Levels)

  • Hands-on paid media experience directly planning, buying, and managing full-funnel paid campaigns across paid search, paid social, and paid video, preferably at a consumer subscription, marketplace, mobile-first, or dating/social platform.
  • Deep, in-the-tool fluency in Google Ads and Meta Ads Manager. Direct hands-on experience with at least one of TikTok, Snapchat, Pinterest, or LinkedIn is expected; multiple is a strong plus.
  • Tracking and analytics expertise. Working knowledge of GTM, GA4, server-side tracking, and CAPI setups. You have built these yourself, not just consumed the output.
  • Strong analytical fluency. Comfortable in Excel/Sheets (pivot tables, VLOOKUPs, data modeling) and in Looker, Tableau, or the warehouse to pull your own reads. SQL is a strong plus.
  • Ready to run on day one. You can audit an existing ad account, identify what is misstructured or wasteful, and ship a better-instrumented campaign in week one.
  • AI fluency. You already use ChatGPT, Claude, or similar in your daily workflow to generate ad copy variants, brief creative, analyze account performance, and replace work you used to do by hand. If someone has to explain to you why AI matters, this role is not for you.
  • Operator's discipline. You ship on time, your QA is tight, your naming is clean, and you document what you did.

Level & Experience

Paid Media Specialist

  • 3 to 5 years of hands-on paid media experience.
  • Proven ownership of monthly ad spends in the $100K to $250K+ range across a mix of channels.
  • Owns execution end-to-end across the channels above with strong optimization and testing instincts. Contributes to channel-mix and budget-shape conversations with the Director.

Sr. Paid Media Specialist

  • 5 to 8+ years of hands-on paid media experience, ideally including time at a consumer subscription business, DTC brand, or top performance agency.
  • Proven ownership of monthly ad spends of $500K+ across a mix of channels, with measurable results scaling spend while holding or improving CAC and payback.
  • Owns both execution and strategy. Drives channel-mix and budget-shape recommendations, brings a point of view on where the next $100K of spend should go, and can defend it to the Director and CMO.
  • Mentors and reviews. Sets the bar for account structure, tracking hygiene, and creative testing standards across the team. Comfortable being the go-to reviewer as the paid function scales.
  • Experience with at least two of: programmatic DSP, connected TV, incrementality testing, geo holdouts, or MMM.

Preferred (Both Levels)

  • Experience inside a consumer subscription business or a top consumer/DTC agency, with a track record scaling spend while holding CAC and payback.
  • Google Ads and Meta Blueprint certifications, or equivalent demonstrated proficiency.
  • Hands-on experience with AI-driven media buying, creative generation, and optimization tools.

Compensation

  • Base salary: $70,000 to $120,000, commensurate with experience and level. The lower half of the band anchors the Paid Media Specialist level; the upper half anchors the Sr. Paid Media Specialist level.
  • Full-time, exempt, fully remote within the US.
  • Health, dental, vision, 401(k), and a standard benefits package.
  • Clear advancement path as channel ownership and budget scope grow.

jobs.title: Sr. Product Manager
jobs.excerpt: Rockstar is recruiting for a company that builds the connective tissue for defense acquisition.
jobs.description:
Rockstar is recruiting for a company that builds the connective tissue for defense acquisition. Their platform lets engineering models, simulations, and digital threads move securely across primes, suppliers, and government program offices, so a system can be tested, trusted, and fielded in months rather than years. They work at the center of some of the hardest problems in defense acquisition: getting the right model, to the right person, at the right classification, at the right time. They are a small, senior team, and every hire changes what the company can do next.

About the Role

The company is a platform for sharing and working on engineering data in highly regulated, no-fail industries, where a mistake can cost a mission, an aircraft, or a life. No single team builds a fighter: the airframe comes from a prime, the engine from one supplier, the radar from another, and the teams are separated by geography, classification level, corporate boundaries, and an ecosystem of software tools. The company keeps their models, simulations, and test results connected so they can move fast and not break things.

They are hiring a Senior Product Manager to own a significant piece of that platform end to end. You'll take a set of features that each solve a real problem and turn them into a product that hangs together, one coherent story for the customer, one coherent roadmap for the team.

This is a role for someone ambitious who wants real ownership. You'll get a problem space, direct access to customers, and a strong engineering team. From there, we expect you to figure out what matters: talk to users, find the shape of the problem, decide what to build and in what order, and carry it through to shipped. You'll work directly with their Head of Product on strategy. Your job is to bring a clear point of view to that conversation, not to wait for one.

The domain is technical and they like it that way. Their users are systems engineers building spacecraft, hypersonic vehicles, and submarines. A single customer problem might span extracting proprietary CAD files into vendor-neutral formats, sharing data across air-gapped environments, and automatically re-checking mission requirements on every revision, which means their product touches engineering tools, SDKs, APIs, workflows, and secure infrastructure. You don't need to be able to administer a Kubernetes cluster, but a conversation about one shouldn't scare you. You need enough technical depth that engineers trust your judgment and customers trust your answers.

You don't need to have run a business or owned a massive roadmap. You do need to be comfortable in a room with senior stakeholders (a customer's chief engineer, a program executive, their leadership team) and able to hold your own.

Core Responsibilities

  • Own a product area end to end: define what success means, build and manage the roadmap, and make the calls on what to build next and what not to build at all.
  • Create coherence: take a collection of features and turn them into a product customers understand and a narrative the company can sell.
  • Do real customer research: get in front of users, understand their workflows and constraints, and turn what you learn into product decisions.
  • Work day to day with a senior engineering team: write crisp specs, make fast decisions when they're blocked, and protect their time from everything that isn't the work.
  • Partner with their Head of Product on strategy: bring the evidence, argue for a direction, and help decide where the product goes next.
  • Communicate with senior stakeholders: engage credibly with customers, sales, and leadership, and represent your area to all of them.

Requirements and Who Thrives in This Role

They hire for judgment, curiosity, and a bias toward action more than for a specific degree or years of experience. That said, people who do well in this role tend to share a few things:

  • 4+ years of product management experience at a company known for shipping excellent product at speed, think Stripe, Ramp, Datadog, or an equivalent high-caliber environment.
  • A track record of shipping under ambiguity: you've taken complicated, ambiguous features from idea to shipped with minimal direction, and you've been handed a hard problem and come back with a good answer.
  • Comfort in technical domains: you've built products for technical users, or products with real infrastructure underneath them, and you can go deep enough to earn an engineer's trust.
  • Strong customer instincts: you'd rather talk to five users than read fifty tickets, and you know how to turn research into decisions.
  • Directness: when asked for your best guess, you give it. You don't hedge, and you'd rather say "we're doing this wrong, here's what I'd do instead" than make people guess what you think.
  • Speed and ownership: you take responsibility for outcomes, not activity, and you move fast enough that the team never waits on you.

Preferred, Not Required

  • Experience as the PM for a CLI-based tool, SDK, or other developer-facing product.
  • Experience as the PM for a desktop or client application: client software is weird in ways that web/SaaS experience doesn't cover, and they'd benefit from someone who has spent time in those trenches.
  • Deep technical experience with cloud or security infrastructure, especially on products sold to engineers (B2B tooling for data processing, cloud services, and the like).
  • Background in aerospace, defense, digital engineering, or other regulated domains.
  • Must be a US citizen living within the United States.

Why Join Us

You will work directly with the executives and engineers building the company, not through layers of process. You will see your work reach real programs and real missions quickly (the products you ship here end up in test events and fielded systems, not slide decks) and you will have room to shape both the product and the product function itself. This is a small team solving a problem that matters, and they are looking for people who want to build the next chapter of it with them.

They've built a team of what they call Wizards: people who bring depth in their domain and range across others, who are collaborative without being deferential, and who genuinely care about what they're building. They celebrate individual contributions, give feedback early and often, and argue about ideas so they can execute together.

There's no room here for hierarchy for its own sake, or for busywork that doesn't move the mission. They are outcomes-driven, and they hold each other to a high standard, with genuine respect for each person's expertise and wellbeing.

Focus is rewarded. Finish is remembered.

Facts are friendly. Even when they are not fun.

Fellowship is fundamental. Make others successful.

Compensation

$145,000 - $190,000 a year

The Manager, Regulatory Affairs – Global Labeling is responsible for developing and executing global labeling strategies for assigned PDx products, with primary accountability for US FDA labeling activities and US Prescribing Information. The role partners with Clinical, CMC, Safety, Medical, Commercial, global Regulatory Affairs and regional Regulatory Affairs teams to ensure labeling is scientifically sound, globally aligned, and supports product development, registration, lifecycle management, and commercialization.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities

Global Labeling Strategy

  • Lead global labeling strategy for assigned products, with primary focus on US FDA requirements and labeling expectations.

  • Provide labeling input to development programs, lifecycle management activities, and regulatory submissions.

  • Ensure alignment between US labeling, CCDS, and regional implementation strategies.

FDA Labeling Leadership

  • Maintain labeling trackers, action logs, decision records, and implementation status to support global visibility and inspection readiness.

jobs.description:
International Fragrance Sourcing Consultant

About the Role

We're looking for someone who knows how to find and buy full-size, genuine fragrance products through the international gray market (parallel/secondary distribution channels) — not directly from brands. You'll build a network of wholesalers, exporters, and distributors around the world, negotiate pricing, and make sure everything we bring in is authentic and properly documented.

This is a hands-on sourcing role for a fast-growing fragrance subscription business. You'll report to the COO and work closely with Purchasing, Quality, and Legal.

What You'll Do

  • Identify and vet international wholesalers, exporters, and parallel-market distributors who sell genuine full-size fragrance (regions like Dubai/UAE, Europe, Singapore, and others as needed)
  • Build direct relationships and negotiate pricing, minimum order quantities, and payment terms
  • Confirm authenticity and traceability of goods before purchase — including checking for counterfeit risk, verifying trademark/import compliance, and working with Legal on gray-market exposure
  • Manage the full sourcing cycle: supplier discovery, sampling, quality checks, purchase orders, and logistics coordination
  • Track import documentation (customs records, bills of lading, certificates of origin) to keep every purchase clean and defensible
  • Monitor pricing trends and excess/closeout inventory across international markets to find the best deals
  • Partner with Quality to inspect incoming full-size product for damage, mislabeling, or spec issues
  • Keep a running supplier scorecard: reliability, pricing, lead times, and any red flags
  • Stay current on brand trademark disputes and legal actions involving gray-market fragrance distributors, and flag risk early

What You'll Need

  • 10+ years in international sourcing, procurement, or supply chain — ideally in fragrance, beauty, or CPG
  • Direct experience with gray-market or parallel-import sourcing (you understand how it's different from authorized distribution, and the legal gray areas involved)
  • A working network of, or ability to quickly build relationships with, international fragrance wholesalers and exporters
  • Comfort reading customs and trade data (bills of lading, import/export records) to vet suppliers
  • Strong negotiation skills and experience managing supplier contracts across currencies and time zones
  • Working knowledge of trademark and parallel-import law as it applies to consumer goods (not a legal expert, but able to spot risk and loop in Legal)
  • Willingness to travel internationally to meet suppliers and inspect goods

Nice to Have

  • Existing relationships with fragrance wholesalers in Dubai, Europe, or Singapore
  • Experience in the fragrance subscription, discount beauty, or off-price retail space
  • A second language (Arabic, Dutch, or another relevant to key sourcing regions)

A Note on What This Role Is

This role sources genuine, authentic full-size fragrance through parallel/secondary market channels — not counterfeit goods. Every supplier and shipment must be vetted for authenticity, and every deal reviewed for legal exposure before it closes.

About Scentbird

Scentbird inspires fragrance lovers to go beyond the ordinary and sample scents that evoke passion, confidence, and the unknown. Our mission is to revolutionize the way we perfume by bringing the ultimate fragrance playground right to your fingertips and offering a digital subscription service that lets members choose from over 500+ designer perfumes each month.

About the Brands:

  • Scentbird: The easiest way for fragrance lovers to discover, try, and buy their favorite scented products without a commitment
  • Deck of Scarlet: Deck of Scarlet is on a mission to break the clean category, redefining what clean fragrances should smell like. Composed entirely of vegan, cruelty-free ingredients, our fragrances bridge the gap between the clean and luxury categories, using the highest eau de parfum concentrations housed in sculptural, eye-catching bottles. You shouldn’t have to choose between being luxe and refined, or clean and vegan—now, you don’t have to.
  • Confessions Of A Rebel: We were born in 2018, holding fast to the idea that the fragrance industry was in dire need of a change. When we looked around, all we saw was a sea of sameness: outdated archetypes of femininity and masculinity paired with unrelatable images of luxury that we had no say in. In truth, we are complex in ways that cannot be contained in the traditional heteronormative stereotypes, existing beyond the binary with raw, unfiltered voices that deserve to be heard.

Our home equity investment product provides homeowners with a fast, simple, and straightforward way to access the equity in their home without taking out a loan or having to sell. By investing alongside homeowners, Hometap offers debt-free cash in exchange for a share of their home’s future value — all without any monthly payments over the life of the investment. Through a combination of financial innovation and best-in-class customer service, Hometap enables people to get more from homeownership so they can get more from life.

jobs.excerpt: Job Overview:Site Navigators II plays a critical role in the comprehensive coordination of site-level activities throughout the start-up phase of a clinical study and potentially through closeout activities as required.
jobs.description:
Job Overview:

Site Navigators II plays a critical role in the comprehensive coordination of site-level activities throughout the start-up phase of a clinical study and potentially through closeout activities as required. Serving as the single point of contact for investigative sites, this role ensures smooth progression from feasibility and initial outreach through to site activation, extending through the maintenance phase of the study as required. A crucial component in meeting the requirements of the Site Navigator II role is ensuring regulatory compliance, robust site management, optimal site support and training, and effective collaboration between the sponsor, CRO, and clinical site staff. This role serves as a local expert in project start-up/clinical activities for a particular country or region, performs work with limited oversight, and acts as a ‘knowledge resource’ to mentor and train junior colleagues if suitable.

Summary of Responsibilities:

  • Oversight of site level tasks associated with efficient site activation in accordance with ICH/GCP guidelines, local regulations, SOPs and project requirements, including collaboration with project leadership and local monitors to collaboratively achieve project milestones while also ensuring patient rights, wellbeing and safety are protected

  • Identifying potential research sites that align with the study's criteria and assessing their capabilities and resources.

  • Conduct initial site outreach, i.e., site engagement, collection of Confidentiality Agreement, and feasibility survey

  • Remote Pre-Study Visits and follow up documentation, including visit preparation, trip report completion, and other documentation as required to support site selection in line with sponsor, protocol, local and country regulations and requirements

  • Support customization and translation of informed consent forms and patient-facing materials.

  • Collect, track and perform a quality review of all essential documents required for effective and compliant study site activation from Site outreach, submissions, greenlight and until site activation. Maintenance and ongoing awareness of site regulatory compliance, supporting IRB/Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) annual renewals, PI change-over, and document expirations will be performed as applicable in accordance with local requirements.

  • Actively participate in team meetings to facilitate study progress and implement action plans for site level risks, underperforming sites, or issues impacting project milestones and escalate issues in a timely manner

  • Support the CRA team in preparing for site initiation visits (SIVs) by coordinating with vendors, supplies teams, and study leads to ensure timely distribution of clinical study supplies, accesses and documents per study team guidance.

  • Responsible for submissions to and liaise with applicable IRB/IEC, Third Bodies (if applicable), and Regulatory Authorities by collaborating with Global Regulatory Submissions Lead (GRSL)

  • Perform initial contract and budget negotiations with the sites, as well as amended where applicable

  • Ensure high quality documents are filed in applicable systems in accordance with SOPs and project requirements and that the Trial Master File (TMF) is updated and audit ready at all times.

  • Track the progress of the start-up process and ensure that the research site meets all requirements and deadlines.

  • Ensure Fortrea is audit ready by completing accurate, timely, and consistent system compliance on an ongoing basis

  • Serve as primary contact for investigative sites and ensure timely delivery in alignment with scope of work/study budget

  • Perform Case Report Form (CRF) review and data validation against source documentation according to protocol and guidelines as applicable in combination with monitoring for site protocol deviations, Serious Adverse Event (SAE) reporting, and all other duties as needed or assigned throughout the course of the study.

  • Perform country and site ICF review/customization, per local requirements

  • All other duties as needed or assigned

Qualifications (Minimum Required):

  • University/College degree (life science preferred), or certification in a related allied health profession from an appropriate accredited institution (e.g., nursing certification, medical or laboratory technology) or 3+ years' work experience in clinical research, including a strong working knowledge of the ICH/GCP guidelines and RA, IRB/IEC regulations.

  • Fortrea may consider relevant and equivalent experience in lieu of educational requirements.

  • In lieu of the above requirement, candidates with a High School Diploma or equivalent AND a minimum of 5 years' work experience in clinical research, including a strong working knowledge of the ICH/GCP guidelines and RA, IRB/IEC regulations will be considered.

  • Fluent in local official language and in English, both written and verbal.

Experience (Minimum Required):

  • A scientific degree and/ or clinical expertise is optimal for this role.

  • Minimum of 2 +year of experience in clinical start-up/ regulatory process (RGO and Ethics submissions).

  • Working knowledge of ICH/GCP, RA, TGA, Belberry, and other applicable regulations/guidelines; familiarity with investigator start-up documents and contract/budgets negotiation process; previous interaction with operational project teams and investigative sites.

  • Demonstrated understanding of research protocol requirements and proven ability to communicate and educate others about them.

  • Effective communication with various stakeholders, including site staff, CRO personnel, and regulatory authorities.

  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines simultaneously, ensuring that all requirements are met in a timely manner.

  • Understanding of relevant regulations and guidelines related to clinical trials and research.

  • Ability to identify and resolve potential issues that may arise during the start-up process.

  • Ability to negotiate contracts and budgets effectively with research sites.

  • Employees will leverage their existing experience and skills to assume additional responsibilities within the broader role. These will be aligned with operational requirements and internal training, without altering the fundamental nature or classification of the position.

Physical Demands / Work Environment:

  • Remote-based work required with possible office presence depending on location

  • Travel requirements: Limited for training only

The Deputy Project Manager / Technical Lead will report to the Project Manager and serve as the second in command for the program, while acting as the technical lead for cybersecurity testing activities.

  • Support executive and audit briefings regarding testing methodology, results, cybersecurity risks, and findings.
  • Support the Project Manager with program management responsibilities and assume Project Manager duties when required.

Required Technical Skills

  • Experience contributing to cybersecurity testing procedures, playbooks, or assessment methodologies.
  • Exposure to detection validation, purple team, or security operations activities beyond configuration based compliance assessments.
  • Experience developing and maintaining cybersecurity testing procedures, playbooks, and evidence standards.
  • Hands on experience performing penetration testing, configuration reviews, cloud assessments, or security control validation.
  • Working knowledge of detection engineering and SIEM effectiveness testing, including common causes of missed detection such as absent telemetry, broken log pipelines, missing detection content, alert tuning, and failed analyst triage.
  • Familiarity with adversary simulation and threat emulation frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, Atomic Red Team, or MITRE CALDERA.

  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate technical activities across multiple agencies and testing environments concurrently.
  • Experience creating testing procedures, scripts, playbooks, and evidence collection methodologies.
  • Strong technical writing skills, including testing strategies, procedures, and technical memoranda.
  • Experience briefing executive leadership and audit personnel on cybersecurity risks and findings.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Experience coordinating technical testing activities.
  • Experience contributing to cybersecurity testing procedures, playbooks, or assessment methodologies.

• CySA+

• GSEC

    • PenTest+

• GCIH

Preferred:

• CISA

• OSCP

  • CRTO
    • GCIA

• PMP

Preferred Qualifications

jobs.excerpt: Backblaze is the object storage leader in the open cloud movement, fueling customer success with cloud storage built purposefully to unlock budgets, unburden administrators, and unleash innovators.
jobs.description:
Backblaze is the object storage leader in the open cloud movement, fueling customer success with cloud storage built purposefully to unlock budgets, unburden administrators, and unleash innovators. Together with our partners, we’re helping customers break free from the restrictive, overpriced legacy solutions that hold them back, and blaze forward with the full power of the open cloud in their hands.

Founded in 2007, we scaled the business with less than $3 million in outside funding until 2021, when we did a traditional IPO on the Nasdaq stock exchange. Today, Backblaze generates over $100m in revenue and is the leading specialized storage cloud - managing over three billion gigabytes of data storage for 500K+ customers in 175+ countries, including businesses, developers, IT professionals, and individuals.

But while there is a lot to celebrate in our past, there is almost as much opportunity ahead of us. We are seeking a: OEM Partnerships Manager!

About the Role:

Backblaze closed CoreWeave at $335M TCV. The NeoCloud flywheel is moving — but it stalls without validated reference architectures embedded at the silicon and systems layer.

This role owns Pillar 1: getting B2 designed-in at NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Cerebras, and the OEM/ODM tier (Super Micro, WD, Seagate) so that every GPU cluster configured for AI inference or training has B2 as the default object storage layer. At the same time we want to build the Storage Tiers from Flash (VAST, WEKA, DDN) to Object Store on HDD with Backblaze. You are the person who makes Backblaze the storage answer before a customer ever talks to a sales rep.

What You’ll Do:

Designed-In at the Silicon Layer

  • Establish and advance Backblaze B2 as a validated storage tier within NVIDIA's AI Data Platform ecosystem — CUDA-integrated, reference-architecture-certified.
  • Drive "Design-In" motions with AMD (Instinct reference stack) and Intel (Gaudi/Xeon roadmap) to close the gap opened by VAST Data's current AMD Instinct reference architecture position.
  • Build relationships with Cerebras, SambaNova, and emerging xPU vendors early enough to be designed into their validated stacks before competitive displacement occurs.

OEM & ODM Tier

  • Own the joint go-to-market with Super Micro (SMCI), WD, and Seagate — turning their hardware deployments into B2-integrated solutions sold as complete infrastructure.
  • Extend these relationships to the Flash Tier - VAST, WEKA & DDN in particular
  • Structure OEM agreements and co-sell motions that create pull-through B2 ARR from hardware-first deals. Build the commercial model (referral, resell, or embedded) for each OEM tier.
  • Identify and close 2–3 new OEM/ODM partnerships per year that generate $10M+ in partner-influenced ARR within the first 6 months.

Turnkey Reference Architectures

  • Deliver 5+ published, co-branded reference architectures by end of FY2026 — pairing GPU compute configurations with B2 as the validated storage layer.
  • Work with the NeoCloud team (Field CTO & BD lead) and DevRel Lead on Flamethrower to produce technical validation content that serves both the partner and the end customer.
  • Ensure reference architectures are submitted to and accepted by Tier-1 analyst firms (2 published analyst reports is a FY2026 OKR.

FY2026 OKR Accountability — Pillar 1

  • Contribute to the $10M TCV OEM-ISV related bookings OKR through OEM-influenced pipeline.
  • Deliver Reference #1 NVIDIA AI Data Platform & OEM (AMD/Intel) co-marketing as Reference #2.
  • Support the 5-of-Top-25 OEM-ISV account close target through OEM-sourced intros and designed-in positions.

Cross-Functional

  • Partner with AEs to convert OEM-designed (powered by) in positions into sourced pipeline.
  • Feed product roadmap gaps (cold storage tier, archive, to Product & Engineering
  • Coordinate with SE (Reference Architectures) so every OEM co-development produces a publishable, reusable asset.

The Right Fit:

Required

  • 10+ years in technology partnerships, alliances, or OEM/ODM business development — preferably in cloud infrastructure, storage, or AI systems.
  • Existing relationships at NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, or a major GPU OEM (SMCI, WD, Seagate, Quanta, or equivalent). You know who owns the ecosystem programs and you can get a meeting.
  • Experience structuring and closing OEM agreements — referral, resell, embedded, or co-sell — with a track record of partner-influenced ARR.
  • Technical fluency in AI/ML infrastructure: you understand GPU cluster architecture, storage tiering, CUDA/software stacks, and how storage fits into training and inference workflows.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive reference architecture co-development — from whiteboard to published, co-branded technical validation.
  • Proficiency with Salesforce for partner pipeline tracking and forecasting.

Strongly Preferred

  • Experience working inside or alongside NVIDIA's AI Data Platform, AMD Instinct, or Intel Gaudi partner programs.
  • Familiarity with S3-compatible object storage in AI data pipeline contexts (training data ingestion, checkpoint storage, inference output).
  • Background at a cloud storage, IaaS, or AI infrastructure vendor (not hyperscaler — we are explicitly the non-AWS/GCP/Azure option).
  • Existing relationships at Cerebras, SambaNova, or other emerging xPU vendors is a significant differentiator.

This Role Is Not For You If

  • You need a mature partner program handed to you — this is a build role. The ref arch playbook exists for CoreWeave; you are extending it to the OEM tier.
  • You lead with slide decks instead of relationships — the first 90 days are relationship mapping and meeting cadences, not program documentation.
  • You are not comfortable with technical conversations at the SE/architect level — OEM partners will disqualify you fast if you cannot hold the storage-in-AI-systems discussion.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience running an AI program across multiple functions simultaneously
  • Familiarity with AI governance in data-sensitive or PII-adjacent environments
  • Background in cloud infrastructure, storage, or technical B2B businesses
  • Exposure to org transitions - restructures, outsourcing programs, distributed team ramp-ups - and the workflow documentation challenges they create

Logistics

  • Remote US · Prefer West Coast or Texas (proximity to NVIDIA HQ Santa Clara, AMD Austin, SMCI San Jose)
  • 30-50% travel · NAB, SC25, GTC, partner QBRs
  • Reports to: Sr. Director, Partnerships & Ecosystem (when filled) or directly to CRO in interim

Backblaze Perks:

  • Healthcare for family, including dental and vision
  • Competitive compensation and 401K
  • RSU grants for full-time employees
  • ESPP program
  • Flexible vacation policy
  • Maternity & paternity leave
  • MacBook Pro to use for work plus a generous stipend to personalize your workstation
  • Childcare bonus (human children only)
  • Fertility treatment and support
  • Learning & development program
  • Commuter benefits
  • Culture that supports a healthy work-life balance

We're transforming the grocery industry

At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Why this role is on the menu

Instacart’s enterprise business is at an inflection point. Retailers and CPG brands are navigating a rapidly shifting grocery landscape—and the demand for Instacart’s ecommerce, fulfillment, in-store, retail media, AI and data solutions has never been greater. We’re hiring a Director of B2B Enterprise Product Marketing to be the strategic engine behind how we bring this platform to market. This role sits at the intersection of product, commercial, and marketing, and the person who fills it will have a direct line of sight to how Instacart powers the future of grocery.

What you’ll cook up in your first year

  • A unified go-to-market strategy for the enterprise platform that is adopted by Product, BD, and Customer Success as the definitive playbook—giving each team clear positioning, messaging, and campaign tools to win deals and grow adoption.
  • A differentiated market presence for Instacart’s enterprise solutions, built through compelling thought leadership narratives, multi-channel campaigns, and industry authority that make Instacart the go-to name for grocery retailers evaluating ecommerce and fulfillment partners.
  • A high-performing, respected product marketing team—four direct reports who are well-integrated into the commercial organization, operating with clarity on priorities, and recognized as indispensable contributors to Instacart’s B2B success.
  • A sales pipeline meaningfully moved by marketing, with awareness and lead-gen campaigns across events, paid media, content, PR, webinars, and partnerships that are measurably converting interest into conversations.
  • A global market entry foundation, with regional strategies developed and tested that support Instacart Enterprise’s expansion beyond existing markets.

The secret ingredients we’re looking for

You are a builder and a storyteller—someone who can translate complex enterprise technology into messaging that resonates with grocery executives, while also rolling up your sleeves to get campaigns out the door. You thrive in ambiguity, love working cross-functionally, and bring a bias toward outcomes over activity.

Must-have pantry staples (Minimum Qualifications)

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills—able to distill complex technical topics into clear, compelling narratives for senior audiences including C-suite

  • Ability to manage multiple high-stakes projects simultaneously, prioritize effectively, and influence cross-functional stakeholders without direct authority
  • Comfortable operating independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with shifting priorities
  • High proficiency with Google Slides and comfort with basic marketing analytics

Optional garnishes (Preferred Qualifications)

  • Experience marketing to retailers or grocery audiences, with an understanding of their unique business challenges and buying cycles
  • Familiarity marketing to a range of company sizes, from large enterprises to SMBs
  • Background in a high-growth startup or scale-up environment
  • Technical proficiency that enables effective partnership with product and engineering teams

jobs.description:
Description

Ledgebrook is seeking a Head of Forward Deployed Engineering to lead the hands-on deployment, scaling, and adoption of production AI and agentic software across our core business units.

In this role, you will lead a high-autonomy team of engineers responsible for embedding directly with operational leaders—from underwriting to finance—to scope, prototype, and ship high-impact AI workflows that business teams actually use. You will serve as the crucial bridge between field reality and our core platform architecture, combining deep technical mastery of modern agentic frameworks (like Claude Code, LangGraph, and CrewAI) with executive business literacy. Exceptional leadership, a builder-first mindset, and a relentless focus on tangible adoption metrics rather than vanity demos are essential for success in this position.

About the Role

What You’ll Do:

  • Embed Across Core Business Units: Run an ongoing, flexible rotation through departments—scoping, prototyping, and shipping production-ready AI use cases alongside business leads rather than following a rigid cadence.
  • Build Reusable Tooling & Accelerators: Develop internal prompt libraries, tool-integration patterns, and retrieval architecture to accelerate subsequent prototype delivery from weeks down to days.
  • Lead a High-Autonomy Engineering Team: Build and guide a small team of engineers, strategically dividing embedded assignments across teams and business priorities while remaining hands-on.
  • Bridge Field Reality and Platform Architecture: Feed key learnings, data classification constraints, and operational realities back into the broader AI platform and tool-selection architecture.
  • Drive Agentic Coding Best Practices: Partner with engineering leads to define quality standards, review/QA discipline, and CI/CD integration points (automated testing, PR reviews, pipeline triage) for tools like Claude Code.
  • Deliver Hands-On Technical & Business Training: Design and execute actionable training and follow-up office hours for engineers and business users that drive real behavior change and adoption.
  • Track Metric-Driven Impact: Measure success through active adoption and business impact metrics per department and engineering team, steering clear of vanity usage stats.

About you

We love working with people who are eager to learn constantly and genuinely excited about the chaotic, rewarding process of building a company from the ground up.

You’ll be a great fit if you bring:

  • A Strong Moral Compass: You believe in doing the right thing, period. We have a strict zero-tolerance policy for toxic behaviors
  • Customer-First Empathy: You are passionate about delivering an exceptional experience to everyone you work with, both inside and outside the company
  • Intellectual Curiosity: You naturally question the status quo and love finding innovative ways to solve problems
  • A Growth Mindset: You possess a hunger for continuous learning and want to constantly expand your skillset
  • Urgency & Prioritization: You can pivot quickly and balance the need to get things right with the speed of getting them done right now
  • A Solution-Oriented Outlook: When things go wrong, you don't look for blame—you immediately focus on how to fix it
  • Transparent Communication: You value honesty, clarity, and open feedback
  • Team-First Energy: You want to win together as a high-performing team and actively build connections across our remote locations

Requirements

Must Haves:

  • 8+ years of production software engineering experience, with recent (last 1–2 years) of deep, hands-on experience using modern agentic/LLM frameworks (e.g., Claude Code, LangGraph, CrewAI).
  • Proven track record of embedding with non-technical business teams to design, ship, and maintain software solutions that teams continuously use in production.
  • Solid CI/CD and DevOps fundamentals, with the ability to evaluate, build, and optimize software delivery pipelines.
  • Strong business analysis skills, capable of translating messy, ambiguous processes (spreadsheets, manual workflows, tribal knowledge) into well-scoped technical solutions without hand-holding.
  • Demonstrated leadership and teaching capabilities, including experience leading small engineering teams in high-autonomy environments while remaining an active builder.
  • High adaptability and business literacy, comfortable operating as the most technical person in a room of operational leaders and the most business-literate person in a room of engineers on the same day.

Nice To Haves:

  • Prior insurance or insurtech domain exposure (e.g., familiarity with actuarial, underwriting, claims, or reinsurance workflows).
  • Experience operating in high-growth startup environments with high tolerance for ambiguity and rapid context-switching.
  • Direct experience establishing data governance, classification, or compliance constraints in production software environments.

Benefits

  • Full remote flexibility and asynchronous work culture
  • Unlimited PTO and fully paid sick leave
  • Comprehensive health benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus HSA and FSA options
  • Additional financial protection and retirement benefits, including a 401(k), company-paid life insurance, and disability coverage

Compensation

  • The base salary range for this position is $200,000-250,000 per year. This is a good-faith compensation range based on what Ledgebrook reasonably expects to pay for this position at the time of this posting. Actual compensation may vary based on a variety of relevant factors including but not limited to experience, qualifications and geographic location

Under the direction of IAM leadership, the Senior IAM Developer provides technical expertise, develops standards, guidelines, and processes for application systems, and translates business requirements into well-designed applicationsbalancing user needs, business objectives, and technical constraints.

This role also involves reviewing system designs and code development for key architectural components, contributing to infrastructure and technology decisions, and participating in regional and national IAM communities to share and expand knowledge.

The Senior IAM Developer will also formulate and define specifications for complex IAM installations, maintenance, and upgrades, while identifying and analyzing performance and capacity issues. The Product Marketing Manager, Platform will own how we position and sell B2 Cloud Storage to business buyers. This is a high-ownership, strategic role on a small, focused team. You will be responsible for the B2 platform narrative end-to-end: what it is, who it is for, why it wins, and how it is differentiated in the market.

B2 serves more than one kind of buyer. Most of your work will focus on our core business audience: backup, media, and general cloud storage use cases. But B2 is also the foundation for a fast-growing set of AI workloads, and you'll partner closely with our AI product marketing lead to make sure the platform narrative holds together as it stretches across both worlds.

You will work closely with the Director of Product Marketing, the sales team, and demand gen to ensure that Backblaze's platform story is sharp, current, and actionable at every stage of the buyer journey.

  • Build and maintain sales enablement materials that sellers actually use: talk tracks, kits, battle cards, and objection handling guides, kept current in real time rather than updated quarterly

  • Building sales enablement materials that sellers used, not just materials that got filed away
  • Operating across multiple use cases and buyer personas without needing a narrow vertical to anchor to
